r: Elected from **Bengal** (Jessore-Khulna) with **Jogendra Nath Mandal**'s support; those districts went to East Pakistan
Re-elected from the **Bombay Presidency**, in the seat vacated by **M.R. Jayakar**
**First Law Minister** of independent India (Nehru's cabinet, 1947)
Monogamy, divorce, inheritance rights of daughters and widows
Minority and Guardianship Act; Adoptions and Maintenance Act
Father / Chief Architect of the Indian Constitution
Law-giver of modern India (Manu = the ancient law-giver, Manusmriti)
14 April 1891 at **Mhow** (now Dr. Ambedkar Nagar, Madhya Pradesh)
Gave evidence demanding **separate electorates and reserved seats** for the depressed classes – his first constitutional intervention
***Mooknayak*** (1920, backed by **Shahu Maharaj** of Kolhapur), ***Bahishkrit Bharat*** (1927), ***Janata*** (1930), ***Prabuddha Bharat*** (1956)
At the **Chavdar tank**; the **Manusmriti** was burnt on **25 December 1927**
Attended **all three** (1930-32) for the depressed classes; Gandhi attended only the second
With Gandhi: separate electorates of the **Communal Award** dropped; **148 reserved seats** in a joint electorate (Award had given 71)
**Independent Labour Party** (1936), **All India Scheduled Castes Federation** (1942)
**Labour Member of the Viceroy's Executive Council** (1942-46)
***Annihilation of Caste*** (1936), ***States and Minorities*** (1947 memorandum – a draft of rights and safeguards), ***The Problem of the Rupee*** (1923)
Chaired the Drafting Committee; sat on the **Fundamental Rights Sub-Committee** (chair **J.B. Kripalani**) and the **Minorities Sub-Committee** under Patel's **Advisory Committee**
Spoke on Nehru's **Objectives Resolution**, urging that the League be brought in rather than forcing the issue
Called the Draft **"workable… flexible and strong enough to hold the country together both in peace time and in war time"**
Moved the third-reading motion **"That the Constitution as settled by the Assembly be passed"**; adopted **26 November 1949**
Gave it in his final speech to **B.N. Rau** (Constitutional Adviser) and **S.N. Mukherjee** (Chief Draftsman)
Article 368 lets Parliament amend most provisions by a special majority – far easier than in the USA or Australia, so no generation is bound
Lost the **1952 Lok Sabha** poll (Bombay North) to **N.S. Kajrolkar**; entered the **Rajya Sabha** from Bombay (1952)
Said he would be **"the first person to burn"** the Constitution if it were misused
Favoured smaller states; suggested **Hyderabad as a second capital** of India
26 November, observed since **2015** – the year of his **125th birth anniversary**
**Dr. B.R. Ambedkar Konaseema district** (renamed 2022); 125-ft **Statue of Social Justice** at Swaraj Maidan, **Vijayawada** (unveiled January 2024)
